clue.text: No engine with coal supplier in Newcastle — I won't dispute that

parts.note: taken as written
a loco is a railway engine, short for locomotive

indicators.note: the coal supplier sits inside the letters standing for Newcastle

parts.note: NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne
a tender is the wagon behind a steam engine that carries its coal

explanation.surface: A steam train without its coal wagon in Newcastle, and someone conceding the point.
explanation.walkthrough: The engine is a steam loco followed by its coal wagon. The Latin plea lets an accused person decline to contest a charge without admitting guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal plea literally means 'I do not wish to contend', so a speaker using it declines to contest the charge.

clue.text: Arabian nights' power upgrade?

parts.note: In the Aladdin tale from the Arabian Nights, a trickster swaps shiny replacements for the hero's worn lamp; 'power upgrade' reads that swap as if it were improving the lighting.

explanation.surface: A question about improving the electricity supply in an Arabian Nights setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The wicked magician in Aladdin walks the streets calling out this offer to trick the princess into giving up the magic lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry offers to exchange shiny replacements for worn lamps, which sounds like an upgrade in lighting.

clue.text: Story about rising model being flexible

indicators.note: the story goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous fashion model

explanation.surface: A tale about a model on the way up who is supple.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' reads the model's surname bottom to top; 'about' sets the story round it. Kate Moss is the British supermodel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is supple and bends easily, a synonym for flexible.

clue.text: Michael confused in irritant gas and the like

definitions.text: Michael confused in irritant gas and the like

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes inside the gas's letters

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used for riot control

indicators.note: the letters of the name are muddled up

explanation.surface: A man called Michael left bewildered amid tear gas and similar substances.
explanation.walkthrough: CS is the British police name for tear gas. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: such gases and their like are all of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas and similar irritants are all manufactured substances of the laboratory sort.

clue.text: Muslin from old widow's place, so that's all right

parts.note: Nain is the town in Luke's Gospel where Jesus raised a widow's son
taken as written
OK means that's all right

explanation.surface: A fabric from the home town of a biblical widow, and an approving remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old widow' is the widow of Nain in the Bible, whose son Jesus brought back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Nainsook is a fine soft cotton fabric, a kind of muslin originally from India.

clue.text: There's no duty to find a river at Minehead Point

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon rising on Exmoor near Minehead
read as 'Mine head', the head of the word mine is M

explanation.surface: A traveller discovering a river at a seaside town in Somerset and finding no tax to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside resort in Somerset; split as Mine-head it gives the first letter of 'mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exempt means being freed from an obligation, such as having no tax or duty to pay.

clue.text: Return of writer's first name

parts.note: read 'of' backwards to get the surname of an Italian playwright; the clue asks for that writer's forename

explanation.surface: A request about the comeback of an author's given name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' gives FO, the surname of Dario Fo, the Italian playwright who won the 1997 Nobel Prize for Literature; his first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel-winning Italian dramatist whose surname reverses 'of' is called by this forename.

clue.text: Rose like a parson in a pulpit

definitions.meaning: a climbing rose with long trailing stems

definitions.text: like a parson in a pulpit
definitions.meaning: a preacher who goes on and on, wandering from the point

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a past-tense verb; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a climbing rose variety and someone who talks at aimless length, as a long-winded preacher does.

clue.text: Where one finds a doctor with an old Ford motoring madly

parts.note: the Ford Consul was a car made from the 1950s to the 1970s

indicators.note: the letters of the word are rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: A doctor driving recklessly in a vintage Ford car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motoring' looks like part of the driving picture but is the fodder for 'madly'. The Consul was a popular British family saloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A GP sees patients in a surgery room set aside for appointments, which is where the doctor is found.

clue.text: It was Tio Pepe, nothing less, poured out here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the zero letter is taken away from the sherry's name
the remaining letters are tipped out into a new order

parts.note: O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bottle of sherry tipped down the sink, every drop.
explanation.walkthrough: Tio Pepe is a brand of dry Spanish sherry. 'less' drops one O from it and 'poured out' mixes the remaining letters; the definition is just 'here', where the wine went.
explanation.definitionFit: The drain from a sink is where unwanted liquid is tipped away, so 'here' points at that outlet.

clue.text: Lover of capital, nothing more

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a city and asks nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' signals that O is added on after the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero gave his name to any ardent male lover.

clue.text: Top grade oil used for Provençal mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: the word's letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Best quality oil going into a garlic sauce from Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top quality) is entered with the figure 1 as I; 'used' rearranges OIL as OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is the garlic sauce of southern France, made like mayonnaise with oil and egg yolk.

clue.text: Old dramatist organises school's PE

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is spelt out, its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An ancient playwright in charge of a school's gym classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organises' rearranges SCHOOLSPE, the S of the possessive included. PE is physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian tragedian who wrote Oedipus the King was a playwright of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Quarry prospector?

parts.note: quarry means hunted prey, not a stone pit, so the 'prospector' is a hunter looking for prey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests a mine; here it is the animal being hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting animal searches out the prey it will kill, a looker for quarry in that sense.

clue.text: Carpet rolled up to reveal a fire hazard

indicators.note: the letters are found running across the two words, revealed within them

explanation.surface: Rolling back a carpet uncovers something dangerously flammable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to reveal' signals the answer sitting inside carPET ROLled.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor fuel is highly flammable, so a can of it is an obvious risk of fire.

clue.text: Wheels rotate before getting away

indicators.note: the letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Wheels spin before a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotate' rearranges WHEELS into ELSEWH, followed by ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be away is to be somewhere other than here, in a different place.

clue.text: Protector of old said to have a name for keener observation?

definitions.text: Protector of old said to have a name for keener observation?

parts.words: Protector of old said to have a name for keener observation
parts.note: the Tudor Lord Protector was Edward Seymour, whose family name sounds like 'see more', a fit name for sharp eyesight

explanation.surface: A question about a historic regent whose name suggests sharper eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Seymour ruled as Lord Protector for the boy king Edward VI; his ducal title is the answer, and his surname is the pun on keener observation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor Protector Edward Seymour held this dukedom, named after an English county in the south-west.

clue.text: Heartlessly eat fish without getting a thing about it

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the fish goes round the other letters
the middle of the word is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone eating fish half-heartedly while avoiding an obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'Heartlessly' strips the middle of 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something means an obsession with it, which is what a fixation of that kind is.

clue.text: One takes payment for advice, of course

definitions.text: One takes payment for advice, of course

parts.words: One takes payment for advice, of course
parts.note: 'of course' seems to mean naturally but points to a racecourse, where someone sells betting advice

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally'; it means advice about the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster sells forecasts of which horse will win, advice for money at the course.

clue.text: A poet could be tricky to resist

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in a tricky way

explanation.surface: Claims that a poet is hard to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be tricky' rearranges TO RESIST. Dante Gabriel Rossetti and Christina Rossetti were Victorian poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel of this family were both noted English poets of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Gypsy gets in a twist

explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges GETS IN A.

clue.text: Nationalist who was good with greeting

explanation.surface: A nationalist leader remembered for being good and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who was' is a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement against British rule.

clue.text: Shameful about establishing one's will

explanation.surface: Something shameful concerning how a will is proved.
explanation.walkthrough: Probate is the court process by which a dead person's will is declared valid.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate person or deed is unprincipled and morally disgraceful.

clue.text: Character of one's years a short time back

clue.text: Twist one taken out of circuit

clue.text: Volume illuminated with a little reading

parts.note: lit means illuminated
a small part of the word reading, its first two letters

clue.text: Reckless character's road speed violation

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, the words violated

explanation.walkthrough: 'violation' rearranges ROAD SPEED; the 's of 'character's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, lawless outlaw ready to take any risk.

clue.text: Stocky cricketer spotlighted

parts.note: Stuart Broad is an England fast bowler
caught in the beam of a spotlight

explanation.surface: A thickset cricketer standing in the spotlight.
